title: Bounded-above complexes resolved by a zero-preserving left resolution
statement: Let $A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], let $C$ be a preadditive category [def-weil-preadditive-category] with a zero object and finite coproducts, and let $\iota:C\to A$ be fully faithful and additive [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor]. Suppose $Q:A\to C$ is a functor preserving zero morphisms and $\pi:\iota Q\Rightarrow\operatorname{id}_A$ is a natural transformation with epimorphic components. On the full subcategory of integer cochain complexes whose terms vanish in all sufficiently large degrees, there are a functor $S$ to integer cochain complexes in $A$ and a natural transformation $a:S\Rightarrow\iota_-$, where $\iota_-$ is the inclusion, such that every $a_L$ is a quasi-isomorphism, every term of $S(L)$ is isomorphic to an object in the essential image of $\iota$, and every upper bound for $L$ is an upper bound for $S(L)$. This functor is defined on all maps in the bounded-above full subcategory, regardless of which upper-bound witnesses are chosen.

proof.text: For a bounded-above $K$ choose any upper bound $b$. [lem-sfb-left-resolution-bicomplex-total-exists] gives the resolution bicomplex, its vanishing for first degree $p>b$ and resolution degree $q>0$, and the existence of both required diagonal totals. The bicomplex and total are the constructions described in that node.

source.place: bicomplexFunctor support and HasTotal instances, lines 48–108

proof.text: Write $T(K)=\operatorname{Tot}(B_K)$ for the total in $C$, and define $S(K)=\iota(T(K))$ by applying $\iota$ termwise. On a cochain map $f:K\to L$, set $S(f)=\iota(\operatorname{Tot}(B_f))$. The functor laws follow from those of the objectwise resolution and total.map. These totals and maps are chosen for the bicomplexes themselves, independently of any bound witness; the bounds only prove that the needed coproducts exist. Thus the construction acts on every map between bounded-above complexes, even with different bounds. If $n>b$, each diagonal summand of $T(K)^n$ is zero: otherwise its indices would satisfy $p\le b$, $q\le0$ and $n=p+q\le b$. Hence the diagonal coproduct $T(K)^n$ is zero. The additive functor $\iota$ preserves zero objects, so $S(K)^n$ is zero as well. For every $n$, the term $S(K)^n=\iota(T(K)^n)$ itself is in the essential image of $\iota$.

source.place: total upper-bound instance, lines 133–149; minusResolutionFunctor and its map_id/map_comp proofs, lines 226–237, followed by termwise application of ι

proof.text: The map $\tau_K$ of [lem-sfb-left-resolution-totalized-augmentation] is natural in $K$ and a quasi-isomorphism: its naturality is the component calculation using $\pi$-naturality, and its quasi-isomorphism is the bounded-column comparison applied to the objectwise quasi-isomorphisms from step 2.

Apply [lem-sfb-left-resolution-additive-total-transport] with $F=\iota$. The category $C$ has a zero object and finite coproducts by hypothesis, $A$ is preadditive because it is abelian, and $\iota$ is additive. The bounds on $B_K$ from step 3 are exactly the two support hypotheses of that lemma. Its natural isomorphism $e_K=\mathrm{mapTotalIso}_{\iota,B_K}$ identifies $\operatorname{Tot}(\iota B_K)$ with $S(K)=\iota(\operatorname{Tot}(B_K))$, naturally for all maps between bounded-above complexes.

source.place: mapTotalIso and its naturality, lines 118–145; bounded-minus support instance in CochainComplexMinus.lean:208–220

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-left-resolution-single-row-total] to identify the total of the row concentrated in degree $0$ with $K$, naturally in $K$.

Write $r_K:\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{singleRow}_0(K))\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ for the isomorphism of step 7. Define $a_K=r_K\circ\tau_K\circ e_K^{-1}:S(K)\to K$. The first and last factors are isomorphisms and the middle factor is a quasi-isomorphism, so $a_K$ is a quasi-isomorphism. For $f:K\to L$, the naturality equations from steps 5–7 give $f\circ a_K=r_L\circ\operatorname{Tot}(\operatorname{singleRow}_0(f))\circ\tau_K\circ e_K^{-1}=r_L\circ\tau_L\circ\operatorname{Tot}(\iota B_f)\circ e_K^{-1}=a_L\circ S(f)$. Thus these components define the required natural transformation; step 4 already proved the essential-image and upper-bound clauses.
